description: Cross-language test vectors shared by stellar-id-core (Rust/Soroban) and stellar-id-client (TypeScript). Generated from the contract test suite (see contracts/identity/src/lib.rs: TEST_CREDENTIAL_CANONICAL, TEST_SIGNING_SEED). The client SDK must reproduce the sha256 and the signature verification result from the canonical string to prove hashing/signing compatibility.
canonicalization: JCS (RFC 8785): object keys sorted lexicographically, no whitespace, UTF-8. The example below is already in canonical form; `input` shows the same credential with keys out of order, `canonical` is the exact byte string that gets hashed.
hashing: SHA-256 over the UTF-8 bytes of the canonical string. The resulting 32-byte digest is what gets anchored on-chain (anchor_credential) and what gets signed.
signing: Ed25519 (ed25519-dalek v2 / tweetnacl-compatible) over the raw 32-byte digest — NOT over the JSON text. Signature is 64 bytes. Test seed [42u8; 32] is a fixed throwaway, never a real key.
note_on_dids: The issuer/subject strings use underscore placeholders (GABC___...), not real strkey addresses — they are opaque example strings here. Only their exact bytes matter for the hash.

ed25519_sign_verify.note: Same as above with the last signature byte flipped (01 -> 00). Any bit flip must fail verification; on-chain this surfaces as a trap, not a return value.
